where: Section 1, paragraph on passing a low input
problem: The source terminal is stated wrongly. With A = 0 V, C = VDD and the output Y at any level above 0 V, the terminal at the lower potential is the input side A, not Y. The source is therefore A, not Y, so VGS = VG − VA = VDD − 0 = VDD, which does not depend on Y. Writing VGS = C − Y makes it look as if VGS falls as Y rises and the nMOS would turn off near VDD, which is exactly what does not happen. A student will carry this wrong picture into the high-level case, where Y really is the source.
fix: When a 0 V is passed, the input side A is the source: VGS = VG − VA = VDD − 0 = VDD, independent of Y. The nMOS stays on for the whole discharge and Y reaches 0 V. Use VGS = C − Y only for the high-level case, where the output Y is the source.

where: Section 3, first paragraph on PTL costs
problem: The sentence 'a passed low through a pMOS alone is |Vtp|' reads as if the low level equals |Vtp| volts from ground without saying so, next to 'a passed high is VDD − Vtn'. The two levels are not written in the same form, so the comparison reads oddly.
fix: Write: a passed high through an nMOS alone stops at VDD − Vtn, and a passed low through a pMOS alone stops at |Vtp| above ground, not at 0 V.

problem: The answer says a TG multiplexer 'can have weak levels'. A transmission gate with full-rail data inputs and a full-rail C bar passes both rails without loss, so weak levels are not the usual drawback of a TG mux. The listed handicap is misleading for a student who has just learnt that a TG restores the rail.
fix: Keep charge sharing, and give the real drawbacks: the output floats (high-Z) when no branch is selected, internal nodes can share charge, and both C and C bar are needed. Say 'weak levels' only for the case where the select signal C or C bar is itself a passed, degraded level. Static CMOS always drives the output to a rail.

problem: 'A long chain of pass transistors adds the drops' is only true when the gate of a later transistor is driven by a passed (already degraded) level. If every gate is held at VDD, each stage stops at VDD − Vtn and the level does not fall further from stage to stage; only the delay grows.
fix: Each stage whose gate is held at VDD stops at VDD − Vtn. Drops pile up only when a later gate or control is itself a passed level, as in some PTL networks. Delay grows with chain length in both cases.

where: Section 1, first mention of the threshold
problem: The symbol Vtn appears in 'The transistor turns off when VGS = Vtn' before it is defined; the definition only comes in the formula box below. English-as-second-language readers on a phone will stumble here.
fix: Introduce it at first use: 'The transistor turns off when VGS = Vtn, where Vtn is the nMOS threshold voltage in V.' Also write γ's unit as V<sup>1/2</sup> rather than V1/2.
